bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Focused brand-building strategy: 76 brands including 32 'Engine Brands' contributing nearly 72% of domestic sales, with brands above INR10 crore sales growing from 32 (MAT Mar-23) to 38 (MAT Mar-26)
- 'Middle of the pyramid' specialty commercial model targeting Consulting Physicians, Medicine Specialists and focused Specialists, capturing 55% of prescriptions from Specialists and 12% from Super Specialists versus IPM averages of 35% and 8%
- Track record of successfully integrating brand acquisitions (from Abbott India, GSK Pharmaceuticals, Sanofi Healthcare India, Bayer Zydus Pharma, Dr. Reddy's) and in-licensing (Ferring Pharmaceuticals)
- Backward integration in hormone APIs via investment in La Chandra Pharmalab Private Limited, which supplies specified hormone APIs under a right-of-first-refusal arrangement, reducing supply-chain risk
- Pan-India distribution network and Medical Representative (MR) team supporting broad market reach
- Consistent outperformance of the Indian Pharmaceutical Market: FY26 growth of 17.18% versus IPM growth of 8.59%, and rank improvement from #32 (2023) to #27 (MAT March 2026) in overall IPM
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Brand concentration risk — Around 76% of domestic sales come from the 32 Engine Brands, creating dependence on a concentrated set of key brands for revenue.
- Therapy concentration risk — High dependence on women's healthcare, cardio-diabetes and pain management segments; revenue could be impacted if demand in these therapies slows or competition increases.
- Geographic concentration risk — West Zone contributes 45.20% of domestic sales, creating regional revenue dependence despite ongoing efforts to expand South and East India coverage.
- API and raw material supply risk — Dependence on third-party suppliers for APIs and raw materials may cause supply disruptions and cost volatility; partly mitigated via backward integration into hormone APIs through La Chandra Pharmalab.
- Regulatory and compliance risk — Pharmaceutical operations are subject to strict regulatory approvals, inspections and price controls across manufacturing facilities.
- NLEM / price control risk — Price controls under the National List of Essential Medicines can compress product margins; Company states NLEM exposure of 9.76% of sales, which it characterises as lower than the industry average.
- Competition risk — Intense competition from both domestic and multinational pharmaceutical companies may affect market share and pricing power.
- Foreign exchange and import risk — Imported inputs and overseas business expose the Company to forex fluctuations and supply disruptions, compounded by the ongoing Middle East conflict's effect on shipping routes and freight costs.

outlook.body: CORONA operates two internationally accredited manufacturing facilities (Bhayla, Gujarat and Solan, Himachal Pradesh) with 11 production lines across both, spread over an aggregate area of 2.83 hectares, producing oral solids. An additional commercial production capacity of 400 million tablets commenced on December 22, 2025 at the Gujarat facility, supported by sustainability initiatives such as solar power generation and zero-liquid-discharge (ZLD) systems. A dedicated hormone manufacturing plant at Gujarat, 'Advancing Women's Healthcare in India' with a stated capacity of 170 million tablets, is proposed to be commissioned in the coming fiscal year, further strengthening the Company's hormonal therapies and backward-integration strategy. Two DSIR-approved R&D facilities are located within the manufacturing units for lean, integrated operations. Under BRSR Principle 2, the Company's capex directed toward environmentally/socially beneficial technologies (including Zero Liquid Discharge systems and effluent treatment plants) rose to Rs.14.54 crore in FY26 from Rs.3.33 crore in FY25.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's medium- to long-term growth outlook remains positive, supported by favourable demographics, urbanisation and expanding access to essential services including healthcare
- Indian pharmaceutical companies are expected to grow by 9-11% in FY26, supported by healthy domestic demand, growth in European markets and stable raw material costs
- Chronic segment continues to form the backbone of IPM growth: cardiac therapies (~14% of IPM value) grew 13.2% MAT, anti-diabetics grew 9.9% MAT, respiratory grew 10.3% MAT
- Indian women's health market expected to grow at a 6.2% CAGR from 2026 to 2033, driven by hormonal infertility, contraceptives and menopause segments
- Union Budget 2026-27 Biopharma SHAKTI programme (INR10,000 crore outlay over five years) aims to position India as a global manufacturing hub for biologics and biosimilars
- Department of Pharmaceuticals plans to increase PLI-scheme production support, with FY27 allocation rising by 2.24%
- Rising air cargo costs and higher crude prices are increasing production expenses for pharmaceutical companies; the Middle East conflict has raised freight and cold-chain logistics risk industry-wide
- Company's own covered market of INR85,588 crore (MAT March 2026) is growing at 11.65%, ahead of overall IPM, offering headroom via active addition of new therapy adjacencies
- Company's portfolio is structurally younger than the market, with 57.39% of portfolio value in the Growth stage versus 36.24% for overall IPM, supporting a longer growth runway
- An active new product pipeline cited as a forward growth driver alongside the specialty-focused, middle-of-the-pyramid commercial strategy
- 13 new products launched during FY26, all within the Company's defined covered market

market_position.basis: India-focused branded pharmaceutical formulation company engaged in developing, manufacturing and marketing products in women's healthcare, cardio-diabeto, pain management, urology and other therapeutic areas, targeting the 'middle of the pyramid' market segment with a specialist-doctor focus. Ranked as the 29th largest pharmaceutical company in India in MAT June 2025 (improved from 37th in MAT June 2022) and 17th largest by market share in its Covered Market based on domestic sales for MAT June 2025 (Source: CRISIL Intelligence Report).

opportunities: Indian domestic formulations market (consumption) expected to grow at a CAGR of 8-9% between Financial Years 2024 and 2029 to approximately Rs.3.3-3.5 trillion by Financial Year 2030, aided by rising incidence of chronic diseases, increased awareness and access to quality healthcare.
New hormone manufacturing facility proposed to be commissioned in Gujarat, expected to commence manufacturing operations during the first quarter of Financial Year 2027.
strengths: Second fastest growing company among the top 30 companies in the Indian pharmaceutical market (IPM) by domestic sales between MAT June 2022 and MAT June 2025; domestic sales grew at a CAGR of 16.77% compared to IPM CAGR of 9.21%.

Diversified portfolio of 71 brands (as of June 30, 2025) across women's healthcare, cardio-diabeto, pain management, urology and other therapeutic areas; targeted therapy areas contributed 68.26% of domestic sales for MAT June 2025.

Pan-India sales and marketing network focused on the 'middle of the pyramid' target market, supported by a field force of 2,671 medical representatives; urban and semi-urban areas contributed 75.11% of domestic sales in MAT June 2025.

Quality and current Good Manufacturing Practices-focused manufacturing facilities (two facilities in Gujarat and Himachal Pradesh, aggregate installed formulations capacity of 1,285.44 million units per annum, 11 production lines) with two DSIR-registered R&D facilities and 103 R&D employees as of June 30, 2025.
Qualified, experienced and entrepreneurial management team supported by marquee investors.

meta.thesis: Corona Remedies delivered FY26 revenue/PAT growth of 17%/33%, outpacing IPM by 2x through volume-led domestic expansion and strategic acquisitions (Wokadine, Bayer). The launch of a dedicated IVF division and biosimilars portfolio positions the company for sustained 15% organic + 25% inorganic growth in FY27, despite transient margin pressure from new division ramp-up.
